Data Availability Sampling for Light Clients. Abstract: Light clients cannot download full blocks. We show how erasure-coded blocks and random sampling let a light client verify data availability with high probability, and evaluate sampling overhead on a 512-node network.

Efficient Data Availability with KZG Commitments. Abstract: We present a data availability layer that commits to block data with polynomial commitments, enabling sampling without fraud proofs. Our implementation reduces bandwidth for rollups by 40%.

Proofs of Storage over Erasure-Coded Data. Abstract: Decentralized storage networks must verify that providers keep the data they are paid for. We design proofs of replication over erasure-coded sectors and analyze their security and cost.

Incentive Design for Decentralized Storage Networks. Abstract: We model storage providers as rational agents and propose a payment and slashing scheme that keeps data durable. Simulations show the network retains 99.99% of files under churn.

A Log-Structured Storage Layer for Decentralized AI Data. Abstract: We describe an append-only log layer with a key-value layer on top, mined by storage nodes via proof of random access, designed for large AI datasets.
去中心化存储数据可用性.pdf
去中心化存储网络中的数据可用性证明。摘要:本文提出一种基于纠删码的数据可用性采样方法,轻节点只需下载少量数据即可验证区块数据可用,并在测试网络上评估了开销。

Pipelined BFT Consensus with Linear Communication. Abstract: We present a Byzantine fault tolerant consensus protocol in the HotStuff family that achieves linear view change and pipelined commits, and report throughput on 100 validators.

DAG-Based Consensus for High-Throughput Blockchains. Abstract: Building on Narwhal and Bullshark, we separate data dissemination from ordering, achieving 150k transactions per second with sub-second latency in a geo-distributed deployment.
A Modular Consensus Protocol: Whitepaper. Abstract: This whitepaper describes the safety and liveness of our BFT consensus for a modular blockchain, validator staking, and slashing conditions.
Fair Transaction Ordering and MEV. Abstract: Validators can reorder transactions to extract value. We propose an order-fairness protocol for consensus and measure how it reduces front-running.

Mind the Gap: Latency of Finality in Proof-of-Stake Blockchains. Abstract: We measure the gap between block inclusion and economic finality across Ethereum and Cosmos chains and discuss its impact on exchanges and bridges.

Decentralized Verifier Networks in LayerZero. Abstract: Cross-chain messaging relies on verifiers. We analyze LayerZero DVNs, their security assumptions, and configurations that reduce the risk of forged messages between chains.

A Survey of Cross-Chain Bridge Attacks. Abstract: Bridges have lost billions to hacks. We classify 30 bridge exploits by root cause, from validator key compromise to message verification bugs, and derive design guidelines.

Trust-Minimized Bridges with On-Chain Light Clients. Abstract: We verify the source chain consensus inside a smart contract on the destination chain using succinct proofs, removing the trusted relayer from cross-chain transfers.
Interchain Message Passing at Scale. Abstract: We compare IBC, LayerZero and Wormhole for cross-chain messaging latency, cost and trust model, and propose a routing layer across bridges.

MemSkill: Reusable Skills for LLM Agents. Abstract: Large language model agents struggle to retain skills across tasks. We introduce a memory architecture that stores reusable skills and evaluate it on three agent benchmarks, improving success rates by 18%.

Memory in LLM Agents: A Survey. Abstract: We survey how language model agents store and retrieve memory, from long context to retrieval-augmented memory and episodic stores, and outline open problems.

Teaching Language Models to Use Tools. Abstract: We train a language model to decide when to call external tools such as search and calculators, improving accuracy on agent tasks without hurting language modeling.

Reasoning and Acting with Language Models. Abstract: We interleave reasoning traces with actions so an LLM agent can plan, act in an environment and revise its plan, outperforming chain-of-thought on interactive tasks.

Agora: A Protocol for Communication Between LLM Agents. Abstract: Agents built on different language models need to talk. We propose a protocol where agents negotiate structured messages in natural language and evaluate it with 100 agents.

Benchmarking Web Agents. Abstract: We release a benchmark of 800 realistic web tasks for language model agents and find that the best agents complete fewer than half, mostly failing at long-horizon planning.
大语言模型智能体的长期记忆机制。摘要:本文研究智能体如何在多轮任务中存储和检索经验,提出分层记忆结构,在三个基准上提升了任务成功率。
Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey. Abstract: We review methods that ground language model outputs in retrieved documents, covering retrievers, rerankers and evaluation of factuality.
Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain QA. Abstract: We learn dense embeddings for questions and passages with a dual encoder and outperform BM25 on open-domain question answering benchmarks.

Long Context or Retrieval? Abstract: We compare feeding entire documents to long-context language models with retrieval-augmented generation on 12 tasks and find retrieval cheaper with similar accuracy.
Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models. Abstract: We present high quality image synthesis using diffusion probabilistic models, trained by denoising, and report FID scores on CIFAR-10 and LSUN.
An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition. Abstract: We apply a pure transformer to sequences of image patches and match convolutional networks on ImageNet classification.
Real-Time Object Detection. Abstract: We frame object detection as a single regression problem from image pixels to bounding boxes and class probabilities, running at 45 frames per second.

Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision. Abstract: We train image and text encoders contrastively on 400 million pairs and show zero-shot image classification across 30 datasets.
